faq.q: How far in advance should I book a boat for Starlite Festival 2029?
faq.a: We recommend booking at least 2–3 weeks ahead, especially for peak dates (mid-August). Popular yachts like the Mangusta 80 and Azimut 58 Flybridge sell out quickly. Last-minute WhatsApp inquiries are possible, but availability is limited.

faq.q: Can I watch the Starlite concert from the boat?
faq.a: No, the concert takes place inland at Auditorio de Nagüeles, not on the water. However, a pre-concert cruise lets you enjoy sunset over the Mediterranean, sip cava, and arrive at the venue relaxed and on time.

faq.q: What if my boat returns after the concert starts?
faq.a: Most charters are 2–4 hours. A 2-hour cruise from 19:00 to 21:00 gives you time to dock, change, and reach Nagüeles by 21:30. For longer cruises, start earlier (e.g., 17:00). We can advise on timing.

faq.q: Do you offer transfers from Puerto Banús to Starlite?
faq.a: We can help arrange a taxi or private transfer from Puerto Banús marina to Auditorio de Nagüeles (about 10 minutes, €15–25). Alternatively, drive or use a ride-hailing app. Parking at the venue is limited.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish VAT (21%). No hidden extras. Just bring your party and enjoy.

faq.q: Can I bring my own food or decorations?
faq.a: Yes, you may bring additional food or decorations (e.g., balloons, banners) as long as they don’t damage the boat. Let us know in advance so we can prepare. Glassware is provided.

faq.q: What happens if the weather is bad on the day?
faq.a: Safety is paramount. If the captain deems conditions unsafe, we’ll offer a full refund or reschedule. Check the forecast 24 hours prior; we’ll notify you of any changes.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a group of 10 going to Starlite?
faq.a: The Azimut 39 (11 pax) or Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax) are excellent for groups. For a premium experience, the Mangusta 80 (12 pax) offers space and a free jet ski. All depart from Puerto Banús.

data.body_html:
The Starlite Festival 2029 transforms Marbella into a global music destination every July and August. While the concerts at Auditorio de Nagüeles draw crowds, the smartest way to begin your evening is with a Marbella boat rental for Starlite Festival 2029. A pre-concert cruise from Puerto Banús lets you trade traffic jams for sunset views, chilled cava, and the gentle swell of the Mediterranean. Here’s how to plan your evening — from yacht choice to timing and logistics — so you arrive at the festival relaxed and ready.

Why a Pre-Concert Cruise Works for Starlite

The festival gates open around 20:00, with headliners typically performing from 22:00 onwards. A 2-hour cruise from 19:00 to 21:00 gives you ample time to enjoy the coast, sip drinks, and still reach Nagüeles by 21:30. You’ll avoid the Golden Mile traffic and instead soak up the last rays of sun over La Concha mountain. All our charters include a skipper, fuel, and a selection of drinks and snacks — no planning required.

Best Boats for a Starlite Pre-Concert Evening

Our fleet ranges from compact speedboats to superyachts. For a group of 6–11, the Astondoa 40 (€749 for 2 hours) or Azimut 39 (€749 for 2 hours) are ideal: both are 12.5m, seat up to 11 guests, and include all drinks and snacks. If you want to impress, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) starts at €4,719 for 4 hours and comes with a free jet ski. For larger parties, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) or Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) offer spacious decks and premium comfort. View the full fleet on our Marbella boat rental page.

Sample Itinerary: Sunset to Starlite

Depart Puerto Banús at 19:00. Head west towards Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés, where the cliffs reflect golden light. Anchor for a quick swim if the water is warm (often 24–26°C in July). Your skipper will serve cava and beer as the sun dips behind the Sierra Blanca. By 20:45, return to the marina. A taxi to Auditorio de Nagüeles takes 10 minutes — you’ll be in your seat by 21:15. Total cost: from €749 for the boat plus a €20 taxi.

What’s Included in Every Charter

  • Licensed skipper (English & Spanish speaking)
  • Fuel for the full itinerary
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks (chips, olives, nuts)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%) — no hidden fees

You can bring your own food or decorations; just let us know in advance. The only extra is a potential taxi to the venue, which we can help arrange.

Timing Your Cruise to Match the Concert

Starlite concerts usually start around 22:00, but doors open at 20:00. A 2-hour cruise (19:00–21:00) is the sweet spot: you’ll catch the sunset, have time to change, and arrive before the main act. For a longer evening, book a 4-hour charter from 17:00 to 21:00 and include a stop for dinner at a beach club like La Plage Casanis or El Chiringuito. If you’re coming from a villa on the Golden Mile, we can pick you up from Marbella Marina instead of Puerto Banús.

How to Book for Starlite Festival 2029

All bookings are handled via WhatsApp for real-time availability. Simply message us with your preferred date, group size, and budget. We’ll confirm the boat and send a payment link. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), the price is fixed at €749 for 2 hours. For larger yachts like the Mangusta 80 or Ferretti 94, we’ll provide a quote. Contact us now to secure your slot — peak dates fill up weeks in advance.
